name: s1-retrofit
notes: Features f01-f02 are complete examples of the format. Every other item must be completed and reviewed, and the suite frozen, before the pilot.

features.title: Homes and retrofit cases
features.story: As a programme officer, I want to register homes and open retrofit cases so that I can see all the work in one list.
rules: A home has a UPRN (a non-empty string of digits, unique), an address (required) and a postcode (required; stored trimmed and upper-case).
A case belongs to one home and one measure: loft insulation, cavity wall insulation, external wall insulation, air source heat pump, solar pv or windows.
A home cannot have two cases for the same measure.
Case ids are C-0001, C-0002, ... in creation order.
list_cases returns cases ordered by id, optionally filtered by postcode prefix (case-insensitive) and by measure.
CSV import (header uprn,address,postcode) is all-or-nothing: if any row is invalid or duplicated, within the file or against existing homes, nothing is imported.
api: add_home(uprn, address, postcode) -> Home with attributes uprn, address, postcode.
open_case(uprn, measure) -> Case with attributes id, uprn, measure.
ValidationError for invalid input and NotFoundError for unknown homes or cases, both importable from workbench.

features.title: Case lifecycle
features.story: As a programme officer, I want each case to move through the retrofit lifecycle so that I know where every case stands.
rules: Stages, in order: candidate, surveyed, designed, ready, installed, handed_over. New cases start as candidate.

A case moves forward exactly one stage at a time. Skipping a stage, staying in the same stage or moving backwards raises InvalidTransition, a subclass of ValidationError. An unknown stage raises ValidationError.
Every move names who made it (by, a non-empty string) and is recorded in the case history as (from_stage, to_stage, by), oldest first. A failed move changes nothing.
list_cases can also filter by stage; stage_counts returns every stage with its number of cases, including zeros.
api: move(case_id, to, by) -> Case; Case gains the attribute stage.
history(case_id) -> list of (from_stage, to_stage, by) tuples.
stage_counts() -> dict from stage to count.

features.status: draft: write 3-5 visible tests, 10-20 hidden tests (including interactions with earlier features) and extend the reference implementation, then set status to ready
features.title: Ownership and handoffs
features.story: As a delivery lead, I want to hand cases between owners so that responsibility is always explicit.
rules: Every case has at most one owner; assign sets the first owner.
Only the current owner may request a handoff; the owner changes only when the recipient accepts. The recipient may decline with a reason.
A case has at most one pending handoff. Handed-over cases cannot be handed off.
list_cases can filter by owner. Acting without permission raises NotAllowed, a subclass of ValidationError.

features.title: Returns and reopening
features.story: As a surveyor, I want to send a case back to an earlier stage with a reason, and to reopen a handed-over case, so that rework is visible.
rules: return_to moves a case to any earlier stage, with a non-empty reason; it is recorded in history like a move.
reopen moves a handed_over case back to installed, with a reason; only handed_over cases can be reopened.
Returning or reopening cancels any pending handoff (F3).
notes(case_id) lists the reasons, oldest first.

features.title: Safety holds
features.story: As a building-safety officer, I want to put a case on hold so that no work proceeds while a hazard is unresolved.
rules: A case on hold cannot move forward (OnHold, a subclass of ValidationError) and cannot be handed off; returns are still allowed.
Only the role building_safety may release a hold (NotAllowed otherwise).
Holds and releases are recorded with who and why.

features.title: Resident consent
features.story: As a resident liaison officer, I want to record consent for each planned measure so that nothing is installed without it.
rules: Moving a case to installed requires consent (ConsentRequired, a subclass of ValidationError).
Withdrawing consent pauses the case: no forward moves until consent is given again. Pause and hold are independent.

features.title: Appointments and no-access visits
features.story: As a scheduler, I want to track offered and confirmed appointments and failed visits so that stuck cases are escalated.
rules: Only offered dates can be confirmed.
Verified no-access visits count; more than five in the active period escalate the case.
Reopening (F4) resets the active counter but keeps the history.

features.title: Roles and field visibility
features.story: As a data protection lead, I want contractors never to see vulnerability reasons or resident contacts.
rules: view_as(role) returns a read-only view with the same read methods.
Contractors never see vulnerability reasons or resident contacts, in any read or export; officers see everything.

features.title: Deterministic priority ranking
features.story: As a programme manager, I want a ranked list of cases with reasons so that crews work on the right homes first.
rules: Ranking follows a versioned policy and returns reason codes.
Held cases come first; ties break by case id.
The same inputs always give the same ranking.

features.status: draft: write 3-5 visible tests, 10-20 hidden tests (including interactions with earlier features) and extend the reference implementation, then set status to ready
features.title: Audit trail and export
features.story: As an auditor, I want a tamper-evident record of every change and a filtered export.
rules: Every write appends an audit entry chained by SHA-256 hashes; verify_audit detects any change to an earlier entry.
CSV export honours the filters of list_cases and the visibility rules of F8.

change_request.title: Regions
change_request.story: As the programme director, I want every home to belong to a region and every user to work within their regions.
rules: Every home belongs to a region; users are scoped to one or more regions.
Lists, ranking, exports and handoffs respect the acting user's regions.
A handoff to a user in another region needs a manager's approval.
api: To be written with the change request's visible and hidden tests.
